finding: §5.2 (modified this round) states "which is why §8.2 excludes this class from mechanize_candidates" — i.e. over-specification is excluded from the emitted mechanize_candidates array. But §8.2 actually excludes it only from branch 3's trigger ("excluded from this branch"; "a recurring over-specification class does not trigger register-a-check and falls through to branch 4") — which implies over-specification DOES recur across recorded rounds and could be IN the array while branch 3 filters it out. A tester asserting on the emitted mechanize_candidates JSON field cannot decide whether it contains "over-specification" when that class recurs (≥2 rounds or ≥5 times in one round): §5.2 says the array omits it, §8.2's "falls through" language is consistent with the array containing it but branch 3 skipping it. Two engineers write contradictory assertions on the same field.
suggestion: Pin one behavior and use identical wording in §5.2 and §8.2: either (a) the mechanize_candidates array never contains over-specification/reviewer-judgement-only classes (array-level exclusion — then §8.2's "falls through to branch 4" should say the recurring class is simply absent from the array), or (b) the array may contain it and only branch 3's next_action selection filters it (trigger-level exclusion — then §5.2 should say "excludes this class from branch 3", not "from mechanize_candidates"). Add an acceptance clause pinning the array's contents for a recurring over-specification class.

finding: §5.2 (modified) says the over-specification finding 'is itself an altitude judgment ... which is why §8.2 excludes this class from `mechanize_candidates`' — asserting exclusion from the `mechanize_candidates` array/signal itself. But §8.2 branch 3 and Test 14 (§11) locate the exclusion one level up, at the next_action branch: §8.2 says a recurring over-specification class 'does not trigger register-a-check and falls through to branch 4', which by the array's own definition (a class recurring in >=2 rounds or >=5 times in one) leaves it a member of the emitted array that merely fails to trigger branch 3. So whether `tp review --record`'s emitted `mechanize_candidates` array includes a recurring over-specification class is contradictorily specified: §5.2 says no, §8.2/Test 14 imply yes-but-non-triggering. This leaves the array's output contract non-deterministic.
suggestion: Pick one level and state it in all three places. Either (a) reword §5.2 to say over-specification is excluded from the register-a-check next_action branch (§8.2 branch 3), not from the `mechanize_candidates` array — matching §8.2 and Test 14 — or (b) make §8.2 explicitly filter over-specification (and any reviewer-judgement-only class) out of the emitted `mechanize_candidates` array so §5.2's wording holds and the array contents are deterministic.

finding: Branch 3 excludes from mechanize_candidates "the canonical `over-specification` class (and any class documented as reviewer-judgement-only)", but the spec defines no data source or mechanism by which tp enumerates the reviewer-judgement-only set. Only one such class (`over-specification`, §5.2) is ever named, and §5.2/Test 14 pin exactly that one literal; the parenthetical "any class documented as reviewer-judgement-only" implies an open, discoverable set (e.g. a role-declared or config-declared marker) that has no home anywhere in the spec — a reviewer authoring a custom role cannot declare a class reviewer-judgement-only, and tp has no field to read it from. An implementer cannot tell whether to hardcode the singleton `{over-specification}` or build a registry, and the exclusion match's normalization (exact string? case-insensitive like §4.1 severity?) is also unstated, so a class spelled `over_specification` would silently fall through to the mechanizable branch.
suggestion: Either (a) state the exclusion set is the fixed singleton `over-specification` in this release (matching §5.2/Test 14 and Non-Goal 2's deferral of an altitude role), and drop the open-ended "any class documented as reviewer-judgement-only" parenthetical; or (b) if extensibility is intended, name the concrete source tp reads (e.g. a `judgement_only: true` flag in `.tp/reviewers/*.json`, recorded via roles_hash) and how the class string is normalized before comparison.

finding: The round-18 clause added to §5.2 states "which is why §8.2 excludes this class from `mechanize_candidates`", asserting `over-specification` is removed from the emitted `mechanize_candidates` array. But the unchanged §8.2 defines that array purely by recurrence ("a finding `class` that recurs across the recorded rounds") with no over-spec carve-out, and excludes over-specification only "from this branch" (branch 3's trigger), explicitly describing "a recurring `over-specification` class" that "does not trigger register-a-check and falls through to branch 4" — i.e. §8.2 treats over-spec as still able to appear in the array while being filtered at the branch. The two changed/unchanged sections now give different accounts of whether `over-specification` is present in the emitted `mechanize_candidates` array (§5.2: removed from the array; §8.2: in the array, filtered at branch 3). Behavior is unaffected (both agree it never triggers register-a-check), so this is a wording/attribution mismatch, not a behavioral contradiction.
suggestion: Align the two accounts. Either soften §5.2 to attribute the branch-level exclusion ('which is why §8.2 excludes this class from the register-a-check branch (branch 3), never triggering it'), or add the carve-out to §8.2's array definition so the emitted array itself omits `over-specification`. Pick one story for whether the class appears in the emitted `mechanize_candidates` array (or note per §10.7 that the emitted membership is an acceptance-level detail).
